a.evidence: A snow layer fills rows 0-4 across the crate. Its scalloped lower edge at rows 3-4 acts as a front-edge line, so it reads as a top surface about 4 rows tall. Below it is a wooden front face from row 5 to row 12, with a dark band at row 9 and a dark base row at 13, about 9 rows in all. The right strip (x 24-30) is a gray, striped, darker panel that reads as a shaded side face. It starts at row 2 and carries a white highlight at row 3, with no separate top of its own. The snow cap shows only a thin top surface, but it meets the 3+ row front-face requirement.

The main wooden body has a white snow heap on top. The heap is mounded in the width profile (row 0 is 12 px wide, row 1 is 20, then 30 from row 2). It runs rows 0-4 at the centre, and its lower edge is scalloped over the brown face. Below it the brown front face runs rows 4-13, with a dark band at row 9 and a dark base at row 13. That gives a top of about 5 rows and a front face of about 9 rows. A separate grey striped panel at the right (x≈24-30, rows 2-13) looks like a side or adjacent block with only vertical stripes and no top surface of its own. This is why all_major_parts_have_top is false.

The main body is a wooden crate (x about 0-23) covered by a white snow heap in rows 0-4. The heap has a scalloped lower edge that drips over the wood at row 4, and it is 3-5 rows deep depending on the column, so it reads as a heap on top (evidence d). Below it the wood front face runs rows 5-13, with a dark band at row 9 and a dark base at row 13. The grey striped panel on the right is drawn face-on with no receding side face. It is a small part and I did not count it as a major part missing a top. This is the most borderline call: the top is only moderately deep, and the snow heap is the only evidence of it.

The silhouette widens from 12 px at row 0 to 20 px at row 1 and 30 px from row 2, so the snow reads as a mound or heap sitting on the crate. It covers rows 0-4, with a scalloped lower edge over the wood at rows 3-4, and I count it as a 5-row top surface (evidence d). Below it, the wood front face runs from row 4 to row 12 with plank bands at rows 5, 9 and 11, and a dark base line at row 13, giving about 9 front rows. The grey striped section on the right, from about x=23 to x=29, looks like a separate side or neighbouring face. The snow's lower edge has no distinct edge line or eave shadow, so the top is not certain, but the heap shape is enough for a three-quarter reading.
